## What You'll Learn

What does it mean to be a global corporation in the 21st century? What dilemmas do business leaders face operating across different political, cultural, technological, and environmental landscapes? Who holds power in the global economy, and how does that shape corporate behavior?

This course uses real cases from companies including **Nike, ExxonMobil, Siemens, Apple, Patagonia, H&M, and TikTok** to analyze the opportunities and challenges multinational enterprises (MNEs) create. Working in teams, you'll bring political, economic, historical, and cultural knowledge to bear on real problems that states and firms face— building skills in:

- Political-risk assessment
- Ethical reasoning about corporate conduct
- Cross-cultural and institutional analysis
- Evaluating how regulation affects corporate strategy

By the end of the term you'll be able to analyze how MNEs generate and confront problems in international contexts, and to assess, diagnose, and propose solutions to them.

---

## How the Course Works

This is an in-person, case-based course that mostly follows a weekly structure:

::: {.info-box}
### {{< fa calendar-day >}} Mondays — framing
Reading discussion, lecture, and concepts. We set up the week's core theoretical, analytical, and empirical themes.
:::

::: {.info-box}
### {{< fa pen-to-square >}} Wednesdays — in-class case write-ups
You work in your team to analyze the week's case and produce a written deliverable *during class*. Come having done the reading. We will try to supplement group work with class discussion/debriefing.
:::
